sentences.text: This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:

ORDER This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to FIR No.32 of 2023 registered at Police Station Indar, District Shivpuri (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376(3) of the I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 7.7.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.18082/2023 with liberty to file afresh after recording of evidence of prosecutrix.
As per prosecution story, the allegation against the present applicant is that he committed rape upon the prosecutrix.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
It is further argued that entire prosecution story is false, fabricated and suspicious.

As per the FIR and statements of prosecutrix, at the time of incident, her parents were arrived at on the spot upon hearing her noise and caught hold the applicant/accused, thereafter, Police came on the spot and arrested the accused.
However, as per the arrest memo, applicant/accused got arrested after three days of alleged incident on 06.03.2023 which falsify the prosecution story.
Further argument is that prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident is also doubtful because in school certificate (Pramanikaran), the father's name of prosecutrix is different.
In Admission Register at serial no.603, the name of prosecutrix's father does not match.
The applicant is in custody since 06.03.2023.
After conclusion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
Trial is going on.
Prosecutrix (PW-1) and her mother and father (PW-2) & (PW-3) have been examined, therefore, the question of influencing them does not arise.
The applicant is having no criminal history.
He is permanent resident of District Shivpuri (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconding or tempering with prosecution case.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
P er contra, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary available on record.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court.
Learned State counsel is directed to send an e-copy of this order to the Station House Officer of the concerned Police Station for information and necessary action.
